body: Tenchu 2: Birth of the Stealth Assassins is Acquire's PlayStation stealth game, first released in North America on 8 August 2000. A prequel to Tenchu, it follows the younger Rikimaru and Ayame alongside their fellow ninja Tatsumaru as the Burning Dawn threatens their world. Missions again reward approaching an enemy without being discovered, using observation and tools to make a dangerous place manageable. The earlier point in the characters' lives gives familiar abilities another context. The player sees how these assassins became the figures introduced in the first game.

Missions take the ninja through varied locations, from farmland and bamboo forests to ships and caverns. The player studies guards, chooses an approach and uses equipment to avoid or quietly remove an obstacle. Performance is ranked after completion, including how often the character was spotted. Better ranks unlock additional gadgets, connecting careful play to new options in later attempts. Returning to a mission can therefore mean improving the route rather than simply finishing it again. A successful run is one in which the plan leaves little opportunity for the enemy to respond.

The Mission Editor allows layouts, characters and objectives to be arranged into a custom assignment. It gives the player a chance to think about stealth from the other side: where a guard should stand, what a route should demand and how an objective should be reached. Noriyuki Asakura returned to compose the music. Activision requested the sequel after the first game's success, and reviewers generally welcomed its refinements. The editor adds a particularly clear extension of Tenchu's design, turning the player from someone reading a guarded space into someone constructing one.
